what_we_found: Says discharge pressure was 'back to 156°F at 14:00'. Discharge pressure is in psig, not °F, and the raw value at 14:00 is 161.3; 156.0 is the 13:00 reading.
implication: Medium: wrong unit and wrong hour.

what_we_found: Reviews say the Plant B C-01 suction-temp sensor 'rails at -395 F when the machine is off'. -395 appears in no controller file; on 06-01 hours 00-07 (C-01 off) the sensor reads 72.9-75.0 F.
implication: Do not build a -395 sentinel rule from the reviews; the exported data does not contain it.

what_we_found: Work order and shift log say C-1 stayed out of service after the 06-09 leak until 07-08. Controller data shows C-01 loaded on 06-10 (39% FLA), 06-25 (65%), 06-28 (15%), 06-30 (76%); the 06-25 review also says C-1 had been running for 15 days. July 1-7 data shows C-01 at 0%.
implication: The June (real) data and the July-Sept (simulated) records disagree about when C-1 was repaired. Treat the 06-10..06-30 C-01 loads as truth for June.

where: Plant B UC-7 Boxing And Dock
what_we_found: Real June data and the 06-30 review say UC-7 recovered on 06-28. The simulated Apr-May and Jul-Sep exports have it dead (459.6 / -459.67) every day, and no work order repairs it.
implication: UC-7 'dead' status flips at the June seams; do not learn a single sensor-health state across all months.

what_we_found: Review cites 5/28 engine room ~95 F avg / 105 F peak, an 8-hour HPR zero on 5/31 and a Back Dock trajectory of 128, 108, 123, 151, 184 F. The simulated May data shows 5/28 engine room 74.6 F avg, HPR avg 29.6% with no zero on 5/31, and Back Dock 195-202 F.
implication: The simulated Apr-May history does not reproduce the real late-May events described in the reviews. June is real; Apr-May and Jul-Sep are simulated.
